directive: When hits are enriched in signal transduction cascades (kinases, adaptors, scaffolds), prioritize untested genes in the same pathway family and in transcription factor families that integrate those signals.

When hits cluster in vesicular trafficking, endosomal sorting, or HOPS complex components, also prioritize untested genes in ubiquitin-proteasome and RNA-binding protein families, as these pathways are functionally coupled.
When hits are dominated by metabolic pathway components (purine metabolism, nucleotide synthesis, cAMP signaling), prioritize untested genes in GPCR and second-messenger signaling families.
When hits include autophagy machinery or lysosomal transport, prioritize untested genes in lipid metabolism, cholesterol trafficking, and ER-lysosome tethering families.
When hits are enriched in transcriptional regulators and cytokine signaling, prioritize untested genes in immune checkpoint, developmental signaling, and chromatin remodeling families.

When hits cluster in Mediator complex, general transcription factors (TFIID/TAF), or histone modification enzymes, prioritize untested genes in the same transcriptional machinery families and proteasome subunits.
When hit rate is moderate (4–5%), use online adaptive (ML-based) selection to exploit emerging patterns; this strategy outperforms fixed heuristics in mid-complexity phenotypes.
When hit rate is very low (<3%) or phenotype involves complex immune regulation (e.g., T-cell exhaustion, CAR-T fitness), use LLM reasoning to integrate domain knowledge and multi-hop pathway logic.
When screening a small, curated gene set with high hit rate (>9%), use LLM reasoning to identify mechanistic links and prioritize genes with pleiotropic roles in essential cellular processes.

When a phenotype involves multi-step cellular processes (trafficking, transcription, metabolism), trust LLM reasoning confidence scores more heavily than raw ML scores, as LLM captures pathway coherence.
When early hits reveal a dominant pathway family, increase confidence in genes sharing functional annotations (complex membership, kinase subfamily, transcription factor family) with those hits.
When screening large genome-scale libraries (>9000 genes), use online adaptive ML in early rounds to rapidly narrow the search space, then switch to LLM reasoning once pathway patterns emerge.
